findings.finding: The plan README still says 'musl's setresuid and setresgid go through __synccall, which signals other threads with tkill, so the broker's W4 child makes the raw syscalls (TR-SETXID)'. In the W4 child, synccall.c:67 takes the single-threaded path, so the child never issues tkill. plan.json's TR-SETXID and the backend README's round-3 F3 disposition ('restated') have both been corrected; this README sentence has not.
findings.requiredChange: Restate the sentence as in plan.json TR-SETXID: the clone3 child makes only async-signal-safe raw syscalls, because __synccall takes __tl_lock (synccall.c:59) and the child runs on the parent's copied libc state.

findings.finding: Round-3 and round-4 probes still accepted by backend_distribution.py: elections are not tied to the owner's recorded elections, so libpathrs electing LGPL-3.0-or-later instead of Q-L's MPL-2.0 passes, as do the MIT OR Apache-2.0 crates electing MIT; and a review's decision attribution is not tied to the review, so glibc attributed to Q-L2 or libgcc to Q-L passes. Gaps in w03_plan.py: an anchor may be any substring of the cited file, so 'the' in amendment.json or in a README passes and a quoted-key anchor proves little; the plan's own README can be cited, as VX-1 does (architecture/w03-plan/README.md:VERIFIER-EXT), even though plan.json cannot; LIC-GATE and TR-SETXID can be dropped without refusal, although Q-L3 and W01-AMEND R4-1 require them.
findings.requiredChange: Tie the owner-named elections (libpathrs MPL-2.0, gmp LGPL-3.0-or-later, compiler_builtins Apache-2.0) and each review's decision to the owner records. Require anchors to be identifiers or quoted JSON keys, or line ranges. Refuse the plan README as a source. Require LIC-GATE and the TR-* obligations to be registered.
